_what: An input is modelled here as a block inside a device record. On some makers it is not part of the device at all: it is a module with its own identity, bought separately, fitted by the owner, and moved between devices. Written 2026-11-24 from MSB Technology and CH Precision, who both say so on their own pages.

_the_evidence.msb: « MSB input modules are a standardized, swappable design that supports all of our DACs. This allows any module to be moved from one DAC to another for seemless upgradeability. » and « Each module uses a toolless lever lock system for modules that allows simple, quick upgrades and replacements. » Eight input modules are listed, including two different USB modules with different ceilings and one of those in two hardware versions.
_the_evidence.ch_precision: « Standard digital inputs include CH-Link HD, AES/EBU, S/PDIF, and Toslink, while optional boards enable high-resolution network streaming over Ethernet and asynchronous USB playback. » and « The third slot may also be configured with an additional Digital HD input board if required. » Here SOME inputs are fitted and others are boards, which is the harder case: the record cannot say which of its inputs the buyer actually has.

_why_it_matters_and_not_only_to_tidiness: Three failures, all of them wrong answers rather than missing ones. ONE: a record states a ceiling for an input the device may not have, so a consumer offered 768 kHz over USB on an MSB with no USB module fitted is told something false about the box in front of it. TWO: the same module's figures have to be copied into every record of that maker - four MSB DACs today, more tomorrow - and a correction to the module then has to find all of them. THREE: one input NAME can carry several ceilings on one device, because the maker sells several modules of that name; this catalogue has one key per interface, so the figures that do not fit are simply lost. MSB alone loses three USB figures and a 32-bit network input this way.
_the_shape_a_fix_would_take: A module is a subject, so it is a record: brand + module name, with its own claims and its own inputs block. A device then holds an assertion that a module CAN be fitted - the same shape as device_match, a row and not a column, many-to-many in both directions, because one module fits many devices and one device takes many modules. What a device record must NOT then do is restate the module's figures, and what a consumer must not do is read a fittable module as a fitted one. A fitted input and a fittable one are different claims and need different words.
_not_decided: Nothing is implemented. This file records the finding and the evidence for it, so that the first person to need it does not have to rediscover it from the maker's pages. The two records that raised it - msb/premier and ch-precision/c1-2 - carry the figures inline today, each with a note saying why that is wrong.
_how_many_makers: Two so far, both high-end, both from today's pass. Berkeley Audio Design is a third case of the same family seen from outside: its DACs have NO USB input and the maker sells the USB interface as a separate BOX rather than a module. The pattern is not a quirk of one firm, and it concentrates at the top of the market, where a chassis is expected to outlive its interfaces.
